cars.variant: Twin H-Power four-door sedan — 1954 USA factory brochure, standard manual reference
cars.specification_market: 1954 USA Hornet four-door sedan with optional Twin H-Power and standard manual transmission. Factory brochure printed pages 4–5, 10–11 and 16 were visually read. Retain advertised 170 hp in its original convention; no modern net conversion. Standard aluminium head is 7.5:1; optional cast-iron head, Hydra-Matic, overdrive and power assists are not assumed. No 7X racing specifications, measured acceleration or verified top speed supplied. Count the original step-down Hornet family once across years, bodies and engines.
cars.summary: The original step-down Hudson Hornet is a historic American performance icon: its low-set chassis and large six-cylinder engine underpinned the Fabulous Hudson Hornet stock-car programme, whose success and enduring cultural recognition extend well beyond the car’s rarity. This production-road representative preserves that lineage without adopting racing hardware.

facts.title: Why this car belongs
facts.explanation: The original step-down Hudson Hornet is a historic American performance icon: its low-set chassis and large six-cylinder engine underpinned the Fabulous Hudson Hornet stock-car programme, whose success and enduring cultural recognition extend well beyond the car’s rarity. This production-road representative preserves that lineage without adopting racing hardware.

media.caption: 1954 Hornet Twin-H four-door sedan photographed by Joe Ross at Hostetler’s Hudson collection in Shipshewana, Indiana, in March 2008. Representative road body with paired intake housings visible under the open bonnet. The photograph does not authenticate exact output, head material, transmission, factory-original equipment or restoration history.
